summary: A fiction excerpt from Book 2, part 49, in which the narrator Cas Russell is questioned by Checker and Tresting about a woman named Dawna Polk, whom he met in Santa Monica. The narrator has little contact information for her, and the two men find only prepaid disposable phone numbers. Their search of driver's license photos for women named Polk turns up no match, so the narrator offers a picture and Checker boasts of his facial recognition software. The narrator's humiliation hardens into anger, and an unsettling inner pain suggests Dawna may have done something to him.
one_line: Cas Russell struggles to trace a woman named Dawna Polk, whom he met in Santa Monica, with help from Checker and Tresting.
key_facts: The narrator, Cas Russell, is asked by Checker whether Dawna has a psych record and responds in confusion.
Tresting suggests the group should look into Dawna, 'Whoever she is.'
The narrator has only Dawna's work number and cell number as contact information.
Checker reports that Dawna's cell number is a prepaid disposable phone.
Checker reports that Dawna's work number is also a prepaid disposable phone.
Checker's search returns driver's license photos of women named Polk with the first name Dawna or Donna.
The narrator concludes that Dawna's face is not among the search results.
Tresting responds to the failed search with 'Color me shocked.'
The narrator suggests using a picture, and Checker says his facial recognition software is the best out there because he wrote it.
The narrator says he met Dawna in Santa Monica at about four p.m. yesterday.
The narrator traces the walking route he and Dawna took on a map of Santa Monica.
The narrator experiences a buzzing pain and an insistent thought that Dawna is all right, which he fights off with a mental crowbar.
The narrator feels embarrassed about his poor background check and angry at being bested by Dawna.
